lesson.text: Remember? A force is a push or a pull, and most of them need touching. Magnets are different: they can pull without touching at all!
A magnet pulls things made of iron, steel or nickel: these are magnetic. Wood, plastic, glass, paper and most other metals, like aluminium, copper and gold, are not magnetic.
Every magnet has two ends called poles: north (N) and south (S). Unlike poles attract: N and S pull together. Like poles repel: N and N, or S and S, push apart.
A magnet's pull works through paper, card, plastic and water, and it is stronger the closer the magnet is. The pull is strongest at the poles.
Make a magnet: stroke a steel needle with one pole of a magnet, many times, always the same way. The needle becomes a magnet. A compass needle is a tiny magnet that turns to point north.
Static electricity pulls without touching too. Rub a balloon on your hair: now it pulls your hair and tiny bits of paper towards it. Rub two balloons, and they push each other apart.

Engineers use magnets to solve problems: fridge doors that stay shut, cupboard catches, and big magnets that lift steel cans out of the rubbish at a recycling centre. What problem could a magnet solve for you?
Try it in the world: at a Science Lab bench, do "Magnetic or not?". Predict each thing first, then test it. Next: light and shadows.

exercises.prompt: Which of these would a magnet pull?
exercises.hint: Magnets pull iron and steel.
exercises.explain: The nail is iron, so the magnet pulls it. Wood, plastic and glass are not magnetic.

exercises.prompt: A magnet pulls a steel paper clip.
exercises.hint: Steel is made mostly of iron.
exercises.explain: True: steel is magnetic, so the magnet pulls the paper clip.

exercises.prompt: What are the two ends of a magnet called?
exercises.hint: The same words are on a compass.
exercises.explain: A magnet's ends are its north pole and its south pole.

exercises.prompt: A magnet pulls a plastic ruler.
exercises.hint: Is plastic magnetic?
exercises.explain: False: plastic is not magnetic.

exercises.prompt: A north pole meets a south pole. What happens?
exercises.hint: Unlike poles attract.
exercises.explain: N and S are unlike poles, so they pull together.

exercises.prompt: Two north poles face each other. What happens?
exercises.hint: Like poles repel.
exercises.explain: Two north poles are like poles, so they push apart.

exercises.prompt: A magnet can pull a steel paper clip through a sheet of paper.
exercises.hint: Does the pull need to touch?
exercises.explain: True: a magnet's pull works through paper, card, plastic and water.

exercises.prompt: Which metal is NOT pulled by a magnet?
exercises.hint: Only a few metals are magnetic.
exercises.explain: Aluminium is not magnetic. Iron, steel and nickel are.

exercises.prompt: Why does a compass needle turn to point north?
exercises.hint: What is the needle made into?
choices: It is heavy at one end
exercises.explain: The needle is a tiny magnet, and the Earth pulls it round to point north.

exercises.prompt: Put these in order, from the weakest pull on a paper clip to the strongest.
exercises.hint: Is the pull stronger near or far?
exercises.explain: The closer the magnet, the stronger the pull: 20 cm is weakest and 1 cm is strongest.

exercises.prompt: Rub a balloon on your hair. What can it pull now?
exercises.hint: Static electricity pulls light things.
exercises.explain: The rubbed balloon has static electricity: it pulls light things like tiny bits of paper and your hair.

exercises.prompt: Tilly's cupboard door keeps swinging open. Which plan uses a magnet to fix it?
exercises.hint: The magnet needs something magnetic to pull on.
choices: a magnet on the door, steel on the frame
a magnet on the door only
exercises.explain: The magnet on the door pulls the steel on the frame, so the door stays shut.

exercises.prompt: At the recycling centre, how can a magnet help?
exercises.hint: Which cans are magnetic?
choices: It lifts steel cans out of the pile
exercises.explain: Steel cans are magnetic, so a big magnet lifts them away from the aluminium cans and glass.

exercises.prompt: Magnet A's N end faces magnet B's N end. Bram turns magnet B round. What happens now?
exercises.hint: After turning, which pole of B faces A's N?
exercises.explain: Now B's south pole faces A's north pole. Unlike poles attract, so they pull together.

exercises.prompt: How can you make a steel needle into a magnet?
exercises.hint: The needle needs to touch a magnet many times.
choices: Stroke it with a magnet, the same way
exercises.explain: Stroking it many times with one pole of a magnet, always the same way, makes the needle a magnet.

exercises.prompt: Magnet A lifts a chain of 7 paper clips. Magnet B lifts 12. How many more does B lift?
exercises.hint: Take the smaller number from the bigger one.
exercises.explain: 12 − 7 = 5 more paper clips, so B is the stronger magnet.

exercises.prompt: Two balloons rubbed on hair push each other apart.
exercises.hint: They have the same kind of charge.
exercises.explain: True: like charges repel, just as like poles of magnets do.

exercises.prompt: Sort them: magnetic or not magnetic?
exercises.hint: Only iron, steel and a few other metals are magnetic.
exercises.explain: Magnetic: the iron nail and the steel paper clip. Not magnetic: plastic, aluminium and wood.

exercises.prompt: Attract or repel?
exercises.hint: Unlike poles attract; like poles repel.
exercises.explain: N and S, or S and N, are unlike and pull together. N and N, or S and S, are alike and push apart.

exercises.prompt: Match each problem to how a magnet solves it.
exercises.hint: Cards 4 and 6 show magnets at work.
exercises.explain: A magnetic catch keeps a door shut. A big magnet lifts steel cans out of the rubbish. A compass needle, a tiny magnet, points north.

exercises.prompt: A magnet is held under a sheet of card. Sort the things: pulled through the card, or not?
exercises.hint: Card does not stop a magnet's pull. Is each thing magnetic?
exercises.explain: A magnet's pull works through card, so the steel clip and the iron nail are still pulled. Wood, aluminium and glass are not magnetic, card or no card.

exercises.prompt: Order the magnets from the weakest to the strongest.
exercises.hint: The more paper clips it lifts, the stronger the magnet.
exercises.explain: Magnet C lifts 3 clips, A lifts 7 and B lifts 12: C is the weakest and B the strongest.
